dsid_ae068ee4aa9640159427cd941bef0238.semantic_summary: This pull request introduces a new multipart/form-data handling feature for the Redwood API's OpenAI-compatibility endpoints. It adds a streaming-safe multipart parser, strict content-type validation with a whitelist, and configurable payload size limits per file and per request. The feature is backward-compatible and controlled by a feature flag. It includes detailed error handling with structured error responses, telemetry metrics for observability, and comprehensive testing (unit, integration, and end-to-end). The rollout plan involves staged enabling via configuration. Reviewers provided feedback on content-type whitelist and error handling improvements, which were addressed before merging.

dsid_9550250a59e74f1bbd5612480b2e7100.semantic_summary: This pull request introduces a server-side streaming timebox mechanism configurable per route to ensure streaming sessions do not remain indefinitely active, providing a deterministic final event when streams exceed a configured time limit. It enhances client Cancel event handling to be idempotent within a resume window using resume tokens containing minimal idempotency metadata, preventing duplicated tool or function executions on reconnect. The implementation includes changes to the stream manager, OpenAI compatibility adapter, tooling for idempotency key persistence, API extensions for streaming event flags, and comprehensive integration tests simulating network disconnects and retries. The feature is guarded by runtime flags and maintains backwards compatibility by default.

dsid_3fd6af404fae48e6b8ea5a57875ef78f.semantic_summary: This design specification outlines the development of interactive tone derivatives and a physics-inspired Kappa elevation scale for data grids and dense UI surfaces. The goal is to algorithmically derive color tokens that maintain accessibility contrast standards and introduce elevation shadows optimized for compact rows. The tokens will be implemented as CSS variables with a compiled fallback, integrated into frontend components like DataGrid and Table behind feature flags, and supported by updated Figma design kits. The rollout plan includes automated accessibility and visual regression testing, a canary release on internal dashboards, and migration guidance to ensure smooth adoption. Key contributors include Ava Martinez (spec creation), Jun Park (engineering review and implementation), Alex Chen (accessibility testing), and Riya Patel (project management approval).

dsid_184be937d34a412ab5e61366d54d8ed6.semantic_summary: This draft specification details extensions to the Policy Engine to upgrade regional failover automation as part of the 2026 Reliability Program. It addresses current gaps in routing policy evaluation by introducing deterministic, auditable decision-making with built-in explainability. The engine will support both recommendation (dry-run) and enforcement modes, consume normalized signals, and enforce safety constraints such as max flips and blast radius limits. Compatibility with architecture decision records ADR-042 and ADR-043 is ensured. The controller remains responsible for execution orchestration. The specification defines new predicates, evaluation modes, signal hierarchy, policy language additions, and output schema to produce a single, stable decision per evaluation.

The analysis identifies subtle political-leaning amplification caused primarily by tokenization normalization changes, with secondary effects from kernel scheduling and KV cache chunking. An ad-hoc rubric was used to score outputs for bias, revealing a drop in neutrality in the newer model. The document includes timeline steps, hypotheses, representative examples, and planned next steps including heatmap instrumentation and mitigation strategies. Collaborators Priya Singh and Lina Patel are involved in follow-up runs. The document is informal, timestamped, and linked to Slack discussions and GitHub PRs for instrumentation.

dsid_c1a6a71323c04c1ba5445aadea340362.semantic_summary: This pull request introduces a token stage cohorting service and a route matrix alerting system within the Redwood observability platform to improve SLO attribution and reduce alert noise. The token_stage_cohort service computes deterministic cohort keys per invocation based on stage-level metrics, enabling grouping of requests by stage footprint. An alert route-matrix generator consumes cohort rollups to emit alert bindings that bias escalation to the most likely pipeline stages responsible for SLO violations. A new dashboard visualizes cohort drift, stage heatmaps, and cost/latency breakdowns to assist oncall engineers in root cause analysis. The feature is rolled out behind a feature flag with low-sensitivity defaults and quiet-window attenuation to mitigate noise. Testing includes unit, integration, and synthetic replay tests. Cohort keys are namespaced by model-major-version to maintain stability across model rollouts.
